symptom: `alter entity M.E modify attribute A: <other EDM type>` on an attribute a published OData service exposes passed `check` and `exec`; `mx check` then reported one CE5016 "Attribute 'A' has type …, but is published as …" per attribute. Measured: String to Integer, Decimal to Integer, Boolean to String, DateTime to String, String to Decimal. String(50) to String(80) was clean.
file: mdl/executor/validate_published_attribute_types.go ValidatePublishedAttributeTypes (MDL102), called from validate_program.go with the lazy project opener. Tests: validate_published_attribute_types_test.go; fixtures mdl-examples/bug-tests/published-attribute-type-change(.fail).mdl
cause: The publisher derives each attribute's EdmType once, when the service is written (mendixAttrTypeToEdm, adjudicated on 11.12.1), and nothing revisits it when the attribute's type later changes. The six earlier CE5016 findings were all that derivation being wrong; this is the derivation going stale.
insight: **When a derived value is stored beside its source, the gap is the edit that changes the source later, and the order of statements in a script decides whether it is a defect.** Measured on MxBuild 11.16.1 in copies of one project that started at 0 errors: `alter` then `create or modify published odata service` is 0 errors (the re-publish re-derives every type); the same two statements the other way round is CE5016. So the rule follows the script in order and clears when a later statement re-publishes, alters or drops the service, and stays silent when it cannot prove staleness. The first version passed its own tests and still missed the re-publish-then-alter case over a PROJECT entity, because the script never declared the attribute so its type was unknown and the entry was dropped: the end-to-end run against the measured scripts found it (9 scripts, all agree after the project-type fallback), the unit tests did not. Enum parameters, `rename attribute` and `drop attribute` (a different CE) are not covered. Sweep: 1,317 repo .mdl files, 0 MDL102 hits. Control: stubbing the check fails the script and project tests; stubbing only the project-type fallback fails the re-publish-then-alter test.
